{{< include _head.qmd >}}

Seven examples from chapter 27 of Edward Aldwell, Carl Schachter and Allen Cadwallader's *Harmony and Voice Leading*: four Bach
chorales, a short progression from C minor to A♭ major in two versions, and an excerpt from Mozart's Trio for Clarinet, Viola and Piano,
K. 498.

How to read the labels and use the scores: [Analysed Scores](index.qmd#reading-the-labels). For modulation itself, see
[Chapter 22](../modulation.qmd).

{{< include _aldwell-schachter.qmd >}}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## For teachers

- **Source:** the notes and analyses are the DDMAL Key Modulation Dataset's encodings of the book's examples (Néstor Nápoles López and
  others), translated automatically to RomanText and copied into When in Rome. `scripts/when-in-rome/build.mjs` reads the MusicXML
  (`src/aldwell`), and every note was checked against music21's reading of the same files.
- **Copyright:** the book is in copyright. The chorales and the Mozart are public domain; 27-4a and 27-4b are the authors' own
  progressions, a few bars each, as encoded in the dataset.
- **Not edited:** the analyses are an automated translation and are shown as they are.
:::

[musictheory.pugetsound.edu/mt21c/Modulation.html](https://musictheory.pugetsound.edu/mt21c/Modulation.html). Tonicization against modulation, closely related keys, diatonic and chromatic pivot chords, and direct, common-tone and sequential modulation.
